steps.tx: Biliary tract malignancies arise from the epithelial lining of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary drainage system. **Cholangiocarcinomas** are anatomically categorized into intrahepatic, perihilar Klatskin tumours, and distal extrahepatic subtypes, with distinct molecular profiles and surgical approaches. Perihilar tumours arise between second-order bile ducts and the cystic duct insertion, distal tumours originate below the cystic duct, and intrahepatic tumours develop within segmental parenchymal bile ductules.

steps.tx: The liver render marks glowing tumors at three drainage points, pairing **intrahepatic ducts** in the parenchyma with the **perihilar confluence** at the hilum and the **distal duct** near the bowel. This matters because the lesson splits cholangiocarcinoma by exactly those anatomic boundaries, each with distinct targets and operations from liver resection to Whipple surgery.
steps.say: The image shows a liver with its branching bile ducts and three glowing tumors along the drainage path inside the liver, at the central confluence, and lower down near the bowel with the gallbladder nearby. It reinforces the lesson map of intrahepatic, perihilar, and distal subtypes that differ in molecular profile and surgical approach.

vis.alt: A liver render shows glowing tumors in small branches plus the central confluence plus the lower duct.
vis.caption: Liver render marking tumor sites along the bile drainage path Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The MRCP shows a tight **perihilar stricture** at the bile duct confluence typical of a **Klatskin tumour**. Bile trapped above the blockage dilates both left and right **intrahepatic ducts**. This upstream widening with an abrupt cutoff is the classic imaging signature of **cholangiocarcinoma** at the hilum.
steps.say: Follow the bright bile channels on this MRCP. Both sides of the liver are swollen with trapped bile, but the main ducts meet at a pinched blockage at the hilum. That abrupt stricture at the confluence is a Klatskin tumour, a perihilar cholangiocarcinoma. Upstream dilatation with a hilar cutoff should make you think of malignant obstruction rather than stones, and tissue diagnosis plus onward referral come next.

vis.alt: An MRCP shows a perihilar Klatskin stricture with dilated upstream intrahepatic ducts.
vis.caption: Hilar stricture with upstream duct widening signals Klatskin tumour. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Systemic immunotherapy combined with cytotoxic doublets defines modern first-line therapy in unresectable or metastatic disease. In the landmark **TOPAZ-1** phase 3 trial, first-line durvalumab combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin significantly improves overall survival in advanced biliary tract cancer. The addition of durvalumab reduced the risk of death by twenty percent, elevating two-year overall survival to twenty-four percent.

steps.tx: The historical chemotherapy benchmark was defined by the British National Cancer Research Institute. **ABC-02** established gemcitabine and cisplatin as the first cytotoxic systemic standard of care for locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract carcinoma in the ABC-02 trial. Compared to gemcitabine monotherapy, the doublet extended median overall survival from 8.1 to 11.7 months without compromising quality of life.

steps.tx: Following curative-intent surgical resection, patients face significant relapse risks necessitating adjuvant intervention. In the **BILCAP trial**, adjuvant capecitabine for 8 cycles following curative resection of biliary tract cancer and gallbladder cancer improves overall survival as demonstrated in the BILCAP trial. In the protocol-specified per-protocol analysis, median overall survival reached 53 months with capecitabine versus 36 months with observation alone.

steps.tx: Precision genomic sequencing in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma reveals targetable kinase fusions. **FGFR2 gene fusions** occur in 10% to 15% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas, successfully targeted by selective FGFR kinase inhibitors pemigatinib and futibatinib. Pemigatinib binds FGFR1-3 and achieved a thirty-six percent objective response rate in the FIGHT-202 trial. Hyperphosphatemia represents an on-target class toxicity requiring dietary phosphate binders.

steps.tx: Somatic metabolic enzyme mutations drive distinct epigenetic dysregulation. **IDH1** R132 mutations occur in up to 20% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas, inhibited by oral mutant IDH1 inhibitor ivosidenib in ClarIDHy. Mutant IDH1 produces the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate D-2-HG, which competitively inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent histone and DNA demethylases. In ClarIDHy, ivosidenib significantly improved progression-free survival in pretreated refractory cholangiocarcinoma.

steps.tx: Gallbladder cancer displays marked geographic variation and female predominance. **Gallbladder carcinoma** is the most common biliary malignancy, highly prevalent in northern India, strongly linked to chronic cholelithiasis, porcelain gallbladder, and anomalous pancreaticobiliary duct junction. Calcification of the gallbladder wall in porcelain gallbladder carries a high malignancy risk, warranting prophylactic cholecystectomy. Early surgical resection with adjacent liver wedge clearance provides the only curative opportunity.

steps.tx: Chronic biliary tract inflammation serves as a major premalignant trigger. **Primary sclerosing cholangitis** PSC is an inflammatory fibrostenotic hepatobiliary disorder conferring an annual 1% to 1.5% incidence of developing cholangiocarcinoma. Over seventy percent of patients have concurrent ulcerative colitis. Surveillance combines annual serum CA 19-9 measurements with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography MRCP to identify malignant strictures before incurable vascular invasion develops.
